newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: 11 feared dead, scores homeless in Colombia storms.
newsitem.headline: 11 feared dead, scores homeless in Colombia storms.

text.p: Storms lashed northeast Colombia over the weekend, killing at least seven people, with four more feared drowned in flood waters, and leaving scores of families homeless, local media said on Sunday.

Worst hit were Santander and Norte de Santander provinces. A vehicle carrying a former mayor, local government officials and their relatives was washed away when a river burst its banks near the town of La Lejia, in Norte de Santander, close to the border with Venezuela, NTC TV news said.
Seven corpses were found but four people were still missing, presumed dead, after the accident which happened during a torrential downpour on Saturday, the programme reported.

In neighbouring Santander province, about 150 people were left homeless after a river flowing through San Vicente de Chucuri flooded, destroying at least 20 houses in the town's red light district. At least 50 people were slightly injured in the incident early on Saturday, Colombia's leading daily El Tiempo reported.
